section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what minimum age can a Wyoming teenager apply for a learner's permit?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Wyoming allows teenagers to apply for a learner's permit at age 15. The permit holder must have a licensed adult (age 21 or older) in the front seat at all times while driving. Wyoming is one of the most rural states in the US, and the 15-year permit age reflects teens' transportation needs in remote areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for drivers age 21 and older in Wyoming?
note: Wyoming sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Commercial vehicle operators face a stricter 0.04% limit. A BAC of 0.08% alone is sufficient grounds for a DUI charge in Wyoming regardless of apparent impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming is an 'open range' state. What does open range law mean for drivers?
options: a:Drivers must yield to all livestock crossings regardless of signs,b:On open range land, livestock may legally roam onto roads, and drivers are responsible for avoiding collisions,c:Only designated highways have open range rules — city roads are excluded,d:Open range means higher speed limits on ranching roads
note: Wyoming's open range laws allow livestock to legally roam freely, including onto public roads. In open range areas, the driver — NOT the rancher — is legally responsible for avoiding a collision with livestock. Watch for cattle, horses, sheep, and other animals on Wyoming roads, especially at night when animals are difficult to see. Open range warning signs indicate these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 sets the illegal BAC at:
options: a:0.00% — any detectable amount,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.05%
note: Wyoming's zero tolerance law sets the illegal BAC at 0.02% for drivers under 21. Any reading at or above 0.02% results in DUI charges and license suspension for underage drivers. Wyoming strictly enforces these laws across the state's vast rural areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Wyoming rural interstate highways?
options: a:70 mph,b:75 mph,c:80 mph,d:85 mph
note: Wyoming's maximum speed limit on rural interstate highways is 75 mph for passenger vehicles. Wyoming's wide-open plains and long straight interstates make it one of the states with higher speed limits. Always check posted signs and remember that weather, traffic, and road conditions may require driving well below the posted maximum.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming is known for sudden, severe wind storms. When driving in high crosswinds on Wyoming's open plains, you should:
options: a:Increase speed to reduce the time exposed to wind conditions,b:Maintain a firm grip on the steering wheel, reduce speed, and be alert for sudden gusts,c:Drive close to large trucks for wind protection,d:Crosswinds have no significant effect on passenger vehicles
note: Wyoming's open plains can produce sudden severe crosswinds that can push vehicles off the road or cause rollovers, especially for high-profile vehicles. In high wind conditions: maintain a firm grip on the steering wheel, reduce speed significantly, increase following distance, and be alert for sudden gusts. The Wyoming DOT posts wind advisories and sometimes closes highways for extreme wind conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Wyoming's GDL program, a learner's permit holder (age 15) must hold the permit for at least how long before applying for a restricted license?
options: a:3 months,b:6 months,c:9 months,d:12 months
note: Wyoming requires learner's permit holders to hold the permit for at least 6 months before applying for a restricted license. During this time, they must complete supervised driving practice with a licensed adult (21+) in the front passenger seat. Wyoming does not have a specific minimum hour requirement for supervised driving, but practice is strongly recommended.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A Wyoming teen with a restricted license (age 16–17) has a nighttime driving restriction. When may they NOT drive without a licensed adult?
options: a:Between 10 PM and 5 AM,b:Between 11 PM and 5 AM,c:Between midnight and 5 AM,d:Between midnight and 6 AM
note: Wyoming restricted license holders under 18 may not drive between 11 PM and 5 AM unless accompanied by a licensed adult (21+). Exceptions include driving to or from employment or school activities. The 11 PM curfew is one of the earlier curfews among US states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Wyoming highway and see cattle on the road ahead. What is the correct action?
options: a:Honk repeatedly to scare the cattle off the road,b:Speed up to drive around the cattle quickly,c:Slow down significantly, come to a stop if needed, and wait for the cattle to move — never try to spook them,d:Flash high beams to alert the cattle
note: When you encounter cattle or other livestock on Wyoming roads, slow down and stop if necessary. Do not honk aggressively or make sudden movements that could spook the animals — a startled cow can weigh 1,000+ lbs and cause serious damage if it charges or panics. Wait patiently for the cattle to clear. In Wyoming's open range areas, this is a common situation that requires patience and caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on Wyoming urban streets when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Wyoming's default urban speed limit is 30 mph when no other limit is posted. Note this is slightly higher than many states which default to 25 mph in urban areas. Always check posted signs — school zones and residential areas may have lower limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming requires vehicles to stop for a school bus with activated red lights. On an undivided road, traffic must stop at least how far from the bus?
options: a:10 feet,b:15 feet,c:20 feet,d:25 feet
note: Wyoming requires all vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with activated red lights. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm retracts before proceeding. On divided highways with a physical median, only traffic behind the bus stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming's Move Over law requires drivers approaching a stopped law enforcement or emergency vehicle with flashing lights to:
options: a:Sound the horn and proceed at normal speed,b:Reduce speed by 10 mph only,c:Move to a non-adjacent lane if safe, or reduce speed significantly if lane change is not possible,d:Stop completely until the stopped vehicle moves
note: Wyoming's Move Over law requires drivers to move to a lane not adjacent to the stopped vehicle if safely possible. If a safe lane change cannot be made, reduce speed significantly. Wyoming expanded the law to cover tow trucks and highway maintenance vehicles in addition to emergency and law enforcement vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming has vast open spaces with long stretches between towns. What is the most dangerous thing to do when you become drowsy on a Wyoming highway?
options: a:Open the windows for fresh air — this is the safest solution,b:Turn on the radio louder,c:Continue driving and fight the drowsiness,d:Pull safely off the road and take a short nap
note: On Wyoming's long, isolated highways, drowsy driving is extremely dangerous. The safest response to drowsiness is to pull off the road at a rest area or safe shoulder and take a short nap (15–20 minutes). Opening windows and loud music provide only temporary and unreliable relief. Drowsy driving impairs reaction time nearly as much as alcohol. Plan long Wyoming drives to include rest stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming requires headlights to be on from sunset to sunrise. When else must headlights be on?
options: a:Only during officially declared weather emergencies,b:When visibility is less than 1,000 feet due to weather conditions,c:Only when driving on highways without street lighting,d:Whenever driving in rural areas regardless of visibility
note: Wyoming requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced to less than 1,000 feet due to snow, fog, rain, or other conditions. Wyoming's weather can change suddenly — from clear blue sky to a ground blizzard in minutes. If conditions limit visibility, use headlights immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming's winter weather includes severe blizzards. If you are caught in a sudden blizzard on a Wyoming highway with near-zero visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving at reduced speed with hazard lights on,b:Follow closely behind a truck to use its wake for protection,c:Pull completely off the road, stay in the vehicle, turn on hazard lights, and wait for conditions to improve,d:Drive back the direction you came from immediately
note: In a sudden Wyoming blizzard with near-zero visibility, pull completely off the road (into a rest area or away from traffic) if possible. Stay in your vehicle — it provides shelter and makes you visible to rescuers. Turn on hazard lights. Wyoming ground blizzards — where wind blows existing snow across roads — can develop instantly and reduce visibility to zero in seconds. Never attempt to continue driving when you cannot see the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal in Wyoming means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Yield to cross traffic without stopping,c:Stop completely, yield to all traffic, then proceed when safe,d:The signal is broken — no rules apply
note: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign in Wyoming. Come to a complete stop, yield to all cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear. A flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution — a full stop is not required for flashing yellow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the recommended minimum following distance in Wyoming under normal conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Wyoming recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On Wyoming's high-speed rural highways (75 mph posted), 3 seconds translates to a significantly longer physical distance. In snow, ice, or wind conditions — frequent on Wyoming's open plains — increase to 6–8 seconds or more.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Wyoming, a solid yellow center line on your side means:
options: a:Passing is permitted when the road ahead is clearly visible,b:Passing is prohibited — do not cross to pass,c:Passing is permitted at speeds below 55 mph,d:Passing is permitted only on divided highways
note: A solid yellow line on your side prohibits passing by crossing the center line. Do not pass when you see a solid yellow line on your side. A dashed yellow line on your side means passing is permitted when safe. Always check your side of the center line before deciding whether passing is legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming's vast distances mean drivers must plan for fuel stops. Which of the following is most important when starting a long drive on a Wyoming highway?
options: a:Set cruise control at the maximum speed limit to arrive quickly,b:Ensure you have adequate fuel — gas stations can be 60+ miles apart on Wyoming highways,c:Wyoming highways have no fuel planning concerns — stations are every 10 miles,d:Only plan fuel stops if driving more than 100 miles
note: Wyoming's rural highways can have gas stations 60 miles or more apart. Running out of fuel on a remote Wyoming road can be dangerous, especially in extreme heat or cold. Always start with a full tank before entering remote Wyoming areas and keep the tank above 1/4 full. Many Wyoming roads have no cell service, making it critical to not run out of fuel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver legally make a right turn on a red light in Wyoming?
options: a:Never — right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:After a complete stop and yielding to all traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Without stopping if no vehicles are visible,d:Only if a green arrow has appeared previously at that intersection
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Wyoming after a complete stop, yielding to all cross traffic and pedestrians. Check for a 'No Turn on Red' sign first. Make a full stop — not a rolling stop — before turning right on red. This rule applies at most Wyoming intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming requires all vehicle occupants to wear seatbelts. What is Wyoming's enforcement type?
options: a:Primary enforcement — police can stop you solely for a seatbelt violation,b:Secondary enforcement — police need another reason to stop you first,c:Advisory only — no fines are issued,d:Required only for front-seat occupants under 18
note: Wyoming has secondary seatbelt enforcement for adults — law enforcement needs another reason (such as speeding or running a red light) to pull you over before issuing a seatbelt violation to adults. However, all children under 9 years old and under 4 feet 9 inches must be in a child restraint system, and violations for children can be enforced separately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming implicitly consents drivers to chemical testing. Refusing a chemical test when suspected of DUI results in:
options: a:No consequence — refusal is a protected right in Wyoming,b:Automatic license suspension and the refusal can be used as evidence,c:A $100 fine with no license suspension for first offense,d:Consequences only if later convicted of DUI
note: Wyoming's implied consent law results in automatic license suspension for refusing a chemical test — 6 months for a first offense. The refusal can be used as evidence in court. Wyoming's large distances and limited public transportation make losing a driver's license especially impactful in this rural state.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Wyoming four-way stop, you and another driver arrive simultaneously. You are heading north; the other driver is heading east. Who has the right of way?
options: a:You (northbound) — you are going straight and have priority,b:The eastbound driver has the right of way because they are to your right,c:You must yield to the eastbound driver because they are on your right,d:Whoever is on the higher-priority road goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right. The eastbound driver is to YOUR RIGHT (from your northbound perspective). You (heading north) must yield to the eastbound driver. Let them proceed first, then continue when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Wyoming rural highway and see a large mule deer in the road ahead. What is the best response?
options: a:Swerve sharply to avoid the deer without braking,b:Brake firmly while holding your lane as straight as possible — do not swerve sharply,c:Flash your high beams and honk to scare the deer away and continue at speed,d:Deer are small enough that hitting one at highway speed is not dangerous
note: Wyoming has a very high rate of deer and wildlife collisions. If a collision with a large animal like a mule deer or elk cannot be avoided, brake firmly while keeping your lane straight. Swerving sharply — especially at highway speeds — can cause you to roll the vehicle or cross into oncoming traffic, which is far more dangerous than hitting an animal. If time permits, brake early and try to stop before reaching the animal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Wyoming has vast distances and remote roads. When should a driver use hazard flashers while in a disabled vehicle?
options: a:Never — hazard flashers drain the battery and make conditions worse,b:When the vehicle is stopped or disabled on or near a roadway to warn other drivers,c:Only when stopped in a designated emergency pullout,d:Only at night — hazard flashers are not needed during daylight
note: Hazard flashers (emergency flashers) should be used whenever a vehicle is stopped or disabled on or near the road to warn other drivers — both day and night. On Wyoming's high-speed rural highways, other drivers may be approaching at 75 mph with limited time to react. In addition to hazard flashers, place emergency triangles or flares behind the vehicle if available, and stay off the roadway while waiting for help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Enter immediately and then adjust speed.,b:Reduce speed to 25 mph before merging.,c:Match the speed of traffic in the acceleration lane and merge when the way is clear.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of traffic on the interstate, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge when there is a safe gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and do not enter slowly and then try to speed up in the travel lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have entered a turn lane to make a left turn and there is oncoming traffic. What should you do?
options: a:Move to the left of the center lane.,b:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,c:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
note: When preparing for a left turn, signal at least 100 feet before the intersection (or more at higher speeds) so other drivers know your intentions. As you wait in the turn lane with oncoming traffic present, keep your front wheels pointed straight. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle only when which condition exists?
options: a:The vehicle in front signals for you to pass.,b:A broken yellow line is on the far side of the centerline.,c:There is a broken yellow line on your side of the centerline.,d:You are in a left-turn lane.
note: Double yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may only pass when the line next to your lane is broken and it is safe and legal to do so. If the solid line is on your side, you must not cross it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road, where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Both on a hill and in a curve.,b:On a hill only.,c:In a curve only.
note: Passing is illegal and unsafe on hills and in curves where your view of oncoming traffic is limited. Only pass on a two-lane road where you have a clear view ahead, there are no signs or markings prohibiting passing, and you can complete the maneuver safely.

question: When you see pedestrians near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Slow down and pass with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, reduce your speed, be prepared to stop, and pass them cautiously. Pedestrians can move unpredictably into the lane, so giving them extra space and time helps prevent collisions.

question: What dangerous outcome is most increased by driver fatigue?
options: a:Getting a parking ticket.,b:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,c:Being late for appointments.,d:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue slows your reactions, harms judgment, and can cause you to fall asleep while driving. When a driver nods off, even briefly, the vehicle can leave its lane or the roadway and crash, often at high speed. This makes falling asleep behind the wheel one of the most dangerous consequences of fatigue.

question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,d:When parked on a level street with a curb.
note: When parking on a hill, you should turn your wheels so that if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic and toward the curb or road edge. On level ground with or without a curb, it is generally safe for the wheels to be pointed straight ahead, but on a slope you must angle the wheels for safety.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because their light aims down at the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Four‑way flashers are for emergencies, not for normal driving in fog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in the left of two lanes going your direction and others are passing on the right, what should you do?
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.,b:Move into the right lane when it is safe.,c:Remain in the left lane regardless of traffic.,d:Increase your speed to stay ahead.
note: The left lane is generally for passing or preparing for a left turn. If traffic is passing you on the right, you are likely going slower than the flow in the left lane. When it is safe, move into the right lane so faster traffic can pass on the left and overall traffic flow stays smoother and safer.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, drivers should use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Hazard flashers only.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, snow, sleet, or fog, use low beam headlights. Their lower, wider beam helps you see the road and makes your vehicle more visible to others without causing as much glare. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and actually reduce how far you can see.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:When trying to move a slow driver along.,b:If you might hit another vehicle.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or to alert others to your presence when needed. Do not honk just to express impatience or to force a slower driver to speed up; that is aggressive and unsafe. It is appropriate to use your horn if you might hit another vehicle or when visibility is limited and you need to warn others. Near blind pedestrians, use extra caution and yield the right‑of‑way; a brief horn tap may be used only if necessary to prevent an immediate collision.

question: What shape and color are most temporary work zone signs?
options: a:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols.
note: Temporary work zone signs are usually orange with black letters or symbols and are often diamond‑shaped, though some may be rectangular. The orange color warns drivers of construction or maintenance ahead so they can slow down and be prepared for changing road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing?
options: a:After you pass the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:Only after signaling three times.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle.,d:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights or front in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until there is plenty of space between you and the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the headlights (or front of the vehicle) you passed in your rearview mirror. This helps ensure you will not cut the other driver off and that you have completed the pass safely.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct initial response?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, the first step is to ease your foot off the accelerator (and off the brake if you are braking). This helps the tires regain traction. Then, look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. Slamming on the brakes or turning off the ignition can make you lose even more control.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian who uses a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:At all times.
note: You must always yield the right‑of‑way to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog. Stop well before the crosswalk and allow them to cross safely, and do not honk or try to rush them. This applies at all times, whether or not a crossing guard is present or the person has already started to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short interstate entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, how should you enter?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a safe gap in traffic before merging.,b:Use the shoulder to get to highway speed before merging.,c:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and then speed up.,d:Speed up on the ramp as you identify a safe gap in traffic and then merge.
note: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, you must wait until you see a safe gap in traffic, then accelerate on the ramp itself so you are close to traffic speed as you merge. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and never use the shoulder as a makeshift acceleration lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Driving at the legal speed limit.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,d:Using public transportation.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or other roadside event—called rubbernecking—disrupts traffic flow, causes sudden slowdowns, and increases the risk of rear-end collisions. Driving at the speed limit and avoiding unnecessary lane changes help keep traffic moving smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street?
options: a:The rightmost lane.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:Any lane as long as it is safe.,d:The center lane only.
note: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, you should begin your turn from the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps turning traffic predictable and reduces conflicts with vehicles going straight or turning right.

question: At a crosswalk, who must yield?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to vehicles.,b:Cyclists always have priority over pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,d:Vehicles must yield to pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked, unless a traffic signal or officer clearly directs otherwise. Yielding means slowing or stopping so pedestrians can cross safely.

question: How close to a fire hydrant may you legally park?
options: a:You may not park within 25 feet of a fire hydrant.,b:You may not park within 30 feet of a fire hydrant.,c:You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.,d:You may park directly beside a hydrant if attended.
note: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant in most U.S. jurisdictions. This space must be kept clear so fire trucks can quickly connect hoses in an emergency.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake as hard as possible immediately.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Turn sharply toward the shoulder.,d:Grip the steering wheel
note: If a tire blows out or goes flat while driving, hold the steering wheel firmly to keep control and avoid sudden movements. Let the vehicle slow down gradually by easing off the accelerator. Once you have the car under control and speed has dropped, brake gently and move to a safe place off the road.

question: When parking uphill where there is no curb, how should you set your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from the roadway instead of into traffic, helping prevent a collision.

question: What are 'no zones' around large trucks?
options: a:Areas that provide sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:Areas with several car lengths between vehicles and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely.
note: No-zones are the large blind spots and danger areas around trucks where the truck driver cannot see you or cannot stop or maneuver safely if you are too close. Staying out of these areas gives the truck driver enough space and visibility to react safely.

question: What behavior is an example of defensive driving?
options: a:Driving with parking lights on during the day.,b:Only focusing on the vehicle directly in front of you.,c:Putting only one car length between you and the vehicle ahead.,d:Keeping your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, behind, and to the sides so you can spot potential hazards early. By keeping your eyes moving and checking mirrors and blind spots, you have more time to react and avoid collisions.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You should speed up to beat the light.,b:You may turn without yielding to oncoming traffic.,c:The protected-turn phase is ending; be prepared to stop and yield.,d:Left turns are prohibited.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected left-turn phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so. If you are already in the intersection, complete your turn with caution, yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,b:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,c:Continue ahead; you have the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Slow or stop early enough so pedestrians can cross safely, and do not proceed until they have cleared your lane and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before you change lanes you should:
options: a:Slow down dramatically,b:Assume other drivers will make room.,c:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,d:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot so you don’t move into a lane already occupied by another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:As soon as you are slightly ahead of the vehicle.,b:When the other driver waves you back in.,c:After you signal for three seconds.,d:When you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, don’t move back too soon. Stay in the passing lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle, including its headlights, in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return safely without cutting the other driver off.

question: If the center of the road has one solid yellow and one broken yellow line with the broken line next to you, what does that mean?
options: a:You are in a passing zone and may pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.,b:You are only allowed to make right turns here.,c:You are not allowed to pass in this area.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe. If the broken line is on your side, you may pass on the left only when there is no oncoming traffic and you can complete the pass safely.

question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Only if you are transporting passengers.,b:When a traffic officer signals you to stop.,c:If there isn’t space on the far side to clear the tracks.,d:Only when the crossing is in a city or town.
note: Never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. If traffic is stopped ahead and you cannot fully clear the tracks, you must stop and wait before the crossing.

question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Use your horn frequently to assert yourself.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit to avoid others.,c:Relax,d:Tailgate slower drivers to express frustration.
note: Staying relaxed and calm helps you avoid aggressive driving. Give yourself extra time, don’t take other drivers’ mistakes personally, and focus on getting to your destination safely instead of “winning” in traffic.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you be prepared for?
options: a:Change lanes only if directed and adjust your speed as needed.,b:Slow down and be prepared for lane changes or closures.,c:Be prepared for workers, slow equipment, and lane changes or closures ahead.
note: Orange construction signs and cones warn of a work zone. You must be ready for workers on or near the roadway, slow or stopped equipment, lane shifts, and reduced speed limits. Slow down, follow posted signs, and be prepared to stop or change lanes safely.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important to do?
options: a:Change lanes frequently.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.,c:Turn on your headlights at all times.,d:Look well ahead of your vehicle to anticipate hazards.
note: At higher speeds, you cover more distance in less time, so you must look farther ahead to spot hazards early. Scanning well down the road gives you more time to slow, change lanes, or stop smoothly if traffic or road conditions change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the speed limit and the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can safely do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed through the intersection without caution.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution without speeding up.

question: What can speed up the elimination of alcohol from the body?
options: a:Eating a large meal.,b:Nothing. Only time will allow all alcohol to leave a person's system.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, showers, or food do not accelerate elimination.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk—stop and allow them to finish crossing.

question: What does double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing allowed from the right only.,b:No passing allowed from either direction.,c:Passing allowed at intersections.,d:Passing allowed from the left only.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe and not prohibited by signs.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.,b:Speed up to regain contact with the road.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply away from the skid.,d:Apply the brakes firmly to regain traction.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. You should ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid braking or making sudden steering movements, because they can cause a complete loss of control.

question: If your tires feel like they have lost contact with the road surface, you should:
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.,b:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,c:Turn the wheel sharply to regain traction.,d:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (such as during hydroplaning), gently ease your foot off the gas pedal and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or turn suddenly; wait until your tires regain traction before adjusting speed or direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, what should you do first?
options: a:Speed up and assume other vehicles will make room for you.,b:Watch only the vehicles in the lane you are entering.,c:Check behind and beside you to see how fast traffic is coming, then adjust your speed to fit into the gap.
note: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, you must first know what is happening behind and beside you. Check your mirrors and blind spots to see how fast traffic is approaching. Then adjust your speed on the entrance ramp so you can merge smoothly into the gap without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: A driver's license is considered a:
options: a:A requirement you must always carry.,b:Right,c:A guaranteed entitlement.,d:Privilege
note: A driver’s license is a privilege granted by the state, not a right or guaranteed entitlement. You must qualify for it, follow the rules to keep it, and it can be suspended or revoked if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: Approaching a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving when they think the kids are done exiting the bus.,b:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Come to a complete stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped. Do not proceed until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is retracted, and it is clearly safe to move, even if the bus has not yet started moving again.

question: Roadways marked with double solid yellow centerlines indicate what about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross them only for limited reasons such as turning left into a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal, but not to pass another vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right, and any pedestrians or cyclists crossing your path.,b:Only pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:No one if they have a green light.,d:Vehicles behind them attempting to pass.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and also to pedestrians and cyclists crossing your path. Even with a green light, you must wait until the intersection is clear and it is safe to complete your turn.

question: Which statement about driving through roadwork zones is true?
options: a:You must slow down in work zones, obey all temporary signs, and be prepared to stop.,b:You can ignore temporary signs if you know the road.,c:You may speed through if no workers are visible.,d:Fines for violations are often higher than under normal conditions.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey all temporary signs and flaggers, and be prepared to stop. Speeds are often reduced and fines are typically higher because workers and changing traffic patterns make these areas especially hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should enter at what speed?
options: a:At the legal speed limit regardless of traffic.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic (as long as it is safe and not above the speed limit). Entering much slower than other vehicles forces them to brake or swerve, which is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Slow down but never stop.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right‑of‑way to any traffic or pedestrians close enough to create a conflict. You only proceed when it is safe and will not force others to change speed or direction.

question: At about what speed can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:Around 35 miles per hour.,c:60 miles per hour.,d:20 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds as low as about 35 mph on standing water, especially with under‑inflated or worn tires. As speed increases, your tires can ride up on the water and lose contact with the road, greatly reducing steering and braking control.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are always fewer vehicles at night.,d:Headlights make it safer so it's not hazardous.
note: At night, your visibility is limited to the area lit by your headlights, making it harder to judge other vehicles’ distance and speed. Reduced visibility also makes it more difficult to see pedestrians, animals, and road hazards in time to react safely.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Maintain a steady speed regardless of conditions.,c:Prepare to stop if needed and adjust speed.
note: As you approach the crest of a hill, you cannot see what is ahead, such as stopped traffic, slow vehicles, or obstacles. You should reduce speed as needed and be prepared to stop so you can react safely to any hidden hazards beyond the hill.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Constantly scanning the environment.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Exceeding posted speed limits and driving too fast for conditions.,d:Driving at the exact same speed as surrounding traffic.
note: Excessive speed is one of the most common contributors to crashes. Driving faster than the posted limit or too fast for weather, traffic, or road conditions reduces your time to react and increases stopping distance and crash severity.

question: Why use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, visibility is reduced. Turning on your headlights (low beams) makes it easier for other drivers to see you, which helps prevent collisions. Many states also require headlights whenever wipers are in use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and signs don't prohibit it.,b:When traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,c:Whenever you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: In many U.S. states, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, you may turn left on red only when turning from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, and only if there is no sign prohibiting the turn. You may not turn left on red from or onto a two‑way street.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When they are clean and dry.,b:Just after it starts to rain.,c:When it has been raining hard for several hours.
note: Roads are most slippery just after it starts to rain because water mixes with oil and other residues on the surface, creating a slick film. After it has rained hard for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction usually improves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, drivers should check:
options: a:Over their left or right shoulder.,b:Only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Only the left outside mirror.,d:Only the backup camera.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; areas not visible in your mirrors are called blind spots. Before changing lanes, you must quickly look over your left or right shoulder to check these blind spots and ensure the lane is clear.

question: If a driver is following you too closely on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Speed up to increase the distance from the tailgater.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down,d:Stop suddenly to warn them.
note: When someone is following too closely, avoid sudden braking or speeding up. If you cannot safely change lanes, gradually reduce your speed to create a safer situation and encourage the tailgater to pass. Smooth, predictable actions reduce the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:They will maintain a perfectly straight line.,c:Expect the unexpected and be prepared to react.,d:The child will always obey traffic rules.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may swerve, stop suddenly, or fail to follow traffic rules. Slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared to react quickly to any sudden movement.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, how should seat belts be used?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Always wear your lap and shoulder belt properly, even in vehicles equipped with airbags, for the best protection in a crash.

question: What must you do when you encounter an octagonal sign?
options: a:Slow.,b:Turn.,c:Stop.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe and after yielding as required.

question: Before backing up your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your high beams to alert others.,b:Rev your engine to warn pedestrians.,c:Close all windows and lock doors.,d:Walk around your vehicle to ensure no person or obstacle is behind it.
note: Before backing, walk around your vehicle when possible to check for children, pedestrians, or obstacles that may be in blind spots. Once in the vehicle, back up slowly while looking over your shoulder and using mirrors to ensure the path is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action is never allowed when you want to change lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,d:Use your turn signal before changing lanes.
note: You should not change lanes while you are actually in the middle of an intersection. Lane changes must be made before or after the intersection, and you must always signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

question: When merging onto the interstate after accelerating and signaling, you should:
options: a:Wait for the entire lane to clear before merging.,b:Stop on the acceleration lane if no gap appears.,c:Merge carefully into the gap.,d:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed because you have the right-of-way.
note: On freeway entrance ramps, use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, find a safe gap, and then merge smoothly into that gap. Do not stop in the acceleration lane unless absolutely necessary, and do not assume other drivers must yield to you.

question: Which statement best describes backing a vehicle?
options: a:Backing is only dangerous when a helper is present.,b:Backing is safe if you only use mirrors.,c:Backing is only risky in large vehicles.,d:Backing is always risky because you have limited rear visibility.
note: Backing is always risky because you cannot see as well behind you as you can in front. Turn and look out the rear window, back slowly, check mirrors, and use a helper when possible to reduce the danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not enter an intersection if doing so will block it when the light turns red:
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Only if directed by a police officer.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.,d:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
note: You should not enter an intersection unless there is enough space on the other side for your vehicle to clear it completely. Even with a green light, entering when you cannot clear the intersection can illegally block cross traffic when the light changes.

question: How can you help the driver behind you keep a safe following distance?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Brake abruptly to get their attention.,d:Flash your lights frequently.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early for turns or lane changes makes your driving predictable. This helps the driver behind you judge distance and maintain a safe following space instead of having to react to sudden changes.

question: If you are getting tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drink something with caffeine.,b:Open a window.,c:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
note: If fatigue sets in, pull over at a safe location to rest, nap, or switch drivers; caffeine is not a reliable substitute for sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers obey at a construction site directing traffic?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,b:Security guards in parking lots.,c:Other drivers with broken-down vehicles.,d:Construction workers off the roadway only.
note: Drivers must obey instructions from flaggers; they direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

question: After drinking several beers, what is the only effective way to reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drink several cups of coffee.,b:Wait; allow time for the body to eliminate the alcohol.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only way to lower BAC; coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do if an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:Pull as far to the right side of the road as possible and stop.,c:Speed up to pass it quickly.,d:Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and siren, you must safely pull as far to the right side of the road as possible and stop, remaining stopped until the vehicle has passed. This allows the emergency vehicle a clear path and prevents sudden conflicts in traffic.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn and be prepared to brake.,b:Begin to prepare to slow down only.,c:Flash your headlights instead of using the horn.,d:Swerve sharply into the next lane to avoid slowing.
note: If a child looks like they may suddenly run into the street, you should immediately give a sharp blast on your horn to warn the child and others nearby, while at the same time being ready to brake or stop quickly. Children are unpredictable, so you must both warn them and be prepared to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What should you do when driving in work zones?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Increase your speed to get through quickly.,c:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey all posted work-zone speed limits and signs, and be ready to stop suddenly. Workers, equipment, and lane shifts can appear unexpectedly, so reduced speed and extra caution are required.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.,c:Passing is allowed only at intersections.,d:Both lanes may pass whenever safe.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles on the side with the broken line may pass when it is safe. Vehicles on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,c:Continue through the intersection
note: If you are already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you should continue through the intersection to clear it. Once you are out of the intersection, pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,b:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,c:Only when you are slowing down.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently—about every few seconds—to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you. Regular mirror checks help you spot fast-approaching vehicles, tailgaters, and changing traffic conditions so you can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a common effect of excessive speed on driving behavior?
options: a:It does not increase crash risk.,b:It conserves fuel on long trips.,c:It often leads to risky decision-making.,d:It increases your ability to react to hazards.
note: Driving too fast reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards and often leads to aggressive or risky choices, such as following too closely or making unsafe passes. Excessive speed also increases crash severity.

question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:After about three seconds no matter what.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When you hear the overtaken vehicle's engine rev.
note: After you pass, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This helps ensure you have enough space and are not cutting too closely in front of the other driver. Always check your mirrors and blind spot before returning to the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian is on the sidewalk.,b:Only when pedestrians are within marked crosswalks.,c:Only if the pedestrian signals you.,d:At all times when necessary to avoid a collision and whenever they are in a crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks and must slow down or stop whenever necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian. Even though pedestrians also have responsibilities, you must always be prepared to yield if there is any risk of a collision, regardless of whether the crosswalk is marked or the pedestrian has signaled.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:
options: a:Pedestrians for traffic law purposes.,b:Hazards that must yield to cars.,c:Illegal on all roadways.,d:Vehicles and must follow the same rules of the road.
note: On the roadway, bicycles are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of motor vehicles. They ride in the same direction as traffic and must signal turns and stops, but they are given extra space and care because they are more vulnerable.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:Only when a police officer signals you to go.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,c:Only if the arrow turns green again after the red.,d:When you are in the proper lane and the way is clear.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed only if you are in the proper lane for that movement and the path is clear of pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles. Other traffic facing a red light must stop, but you still must check that the intersection is safe before moving.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,d:Passing rules depend on the posted speed limit.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the dashed line. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass. This marking is used where visibility or conditions make passing safe in one direction but not the other.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Brake hard and steer sharply toward the right edge of the roadway.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel to maintain control, ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, and let the vehicle slow down gradually before steering to a safe place off the road.

question: What is true about bicycles on the roadway?
options: a:They are restricted to sidewalks only.,b:They must always yield to motor vehicles.,c:They are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,d:They do not follow road rules.
note: Bicycles on the roadway are treated as vehicles. Cyclists generally must obey the same traffic laws and signals as drivers and have the same rights to use the road, while also following any bicycle-specific rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you not assume?
options: a:That they will allow you to pass if you signal.,b:That they will maintain a constant speed.,c:That the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
note: When passing, you should not assume the other driver will help you by changing speed, moving over, or making space. Only pass when you are sure you have enough clear distance, can safely return to your lane, and can complete the maneuver without relying on the other driver’s actions.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then proceed in arrow direction.,b:Proceed immediately without checking for pedestrians.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Stop until the arrow turns off.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection before proceeding.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait; allow time for the body to metabolize alcohol.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake but do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on an interstate?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:If you miss your exit, go to the next exit and re-route.
note: On interstates, you must always signal before changing lanes, keep slower traffic to the right, and continue to the next exit if you miss yours rather than stopping or backing up. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and illegal, so it is not a safe practice.

question: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:No passing zone.,b:Right turns only.,c:Right turns permitted.
note: A yellow pennant-shaped sign, usually placed on the left side of the road, marks the beginning of a no-passing zone. It warns drivers that passing is not allowed in that area because of limited visibility or other hazards.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: On slippery roads, you reduce the chance of skidding by slowing down before you enter curves and intersections, then steering and braking gently. Braking or turning suddenly while already in the curve can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid.

question: What should a driver watch while operating a vehicle?
options: a:Ahead and by frequently checking mirrors and side areas.,b:Only directly in front of the vehicle.,c:The dashboard instruments exclusively.,d:Only the rearview mirror.
note: Safe drivers primarily watch well ahead to see what is coming, but they also regularly check mirrors and the area to the sides. By scanning ahead and around the vehicle, you can spot hazards early and have more time to react.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding left, what steering action should you take?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer left to recover alignment.,c:Steer right immediately.,d:Apply the parking brake.
note: If the rear of your car begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, you steer left to help realign the vehicle with your intended path, then straighten the wheel as you regain control.

question: When traveling at high speeds, how long before a lane change or turn should you signal?
options: a:One second.,b:Four to five seconds.,c:Two to three seconds.
note: At higher speeds you should signal earlier than at low speeds, but typical guidance is to signal at least 100 feet in advance in town and 200–300 feet on highways, which usually works out to about two to three seconds before changing lanes or turning. Signaling too late does not give others time to react, and signaling extremely early can confuse other drivers about your intentions.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Slow down.,c:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to reduce the risk is to slow down on wet roads, especially during heavy rain or when water is pooling. Good tires and avoiding sudden steering or braking also help prevent hydroplaning.

question: Is it legal to have open containers of alcohol while in a motor vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Yes — passengers may drink but drivers may not.,b:Yes — as long as the vehicle is not moving.,c:Only if you are under 21.,d:No — it is generally illegal to drink from or possess open containers of alcohol in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public roadway.
note: Open containers and drinking alcohol in a vehicle on a highway are prohibited; drivers and passengers may face penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are repeatedly being passed while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to match the fastest cars.,b:Move to the left lane immediately.,c:Stay in the center lane regardless.,d:Move to the right lane when it is safe.
note: On multi-lane highways, the right lane is for slower traffic, the left lane is for passing, and the center lane is for through traffic at the normal speed of traffic. If many vehicles are passing you while you are in the center lane, you are likely going slower than the flow and should move safely to the right lane so faster traffic can pass on your left.

question: A school bus ahead in your lane is stopped with red lights flashing. You should:
options: a:Stop and proceed when you believe all children have exited.,b:Pass if you see no children nearby.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,d:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing; proceed only after the lights stop and it is safe to do so.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This protects children who may be crossing the road in front of or behind the bus. Many states allow an exception for oncoming traffic on a divided highway with a physical median, but if you are behind the bus in the same lane or direction, you must always stop.

question: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you hit a parked car and cannot locate the owner, you are required to stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a clearly visible note with your name, address, and contact information. In many states you must also promptly report the collision to law enforcement. This ensures the owner can reach you to handle damages properly.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It can take your eyes, mind, and sometimes hands away from the driving task.,b:It draws the attention of other drivers.,c:It occupies the driver's hands.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it distracts you in three ways: it takes your eyes off the road, your mind off driving, and often one or both hands off the wheel. Even hands‑free calls can be mentally distracting, and holding the phone further reduces your control of the vehicle.

question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Only use the outside rearview mirror.,c:Check over your shoulders.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots. Use your mirrors first, then look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear before steering.

question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do before the curve?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.,c:Maintain freeway speed until the curve is complete.,d:Increase speed to avoid holding up traffic.
note: On a downhill, curved exit ramp, you should reduce speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve, especially going downhill, can cause you to lose traction and skid. Enter the ramp at a safe speed so you can steer smoothly through the curve.

question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has flashing red lights, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass the bus.,b:Proceed at normal speed if you see no children.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing.,d:Slow down to 10 mph and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Children may be crossing the road unexpectedly, so you cannot pass the bus during this time, even if you do not immediately see any children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever legal to drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.,d:If the shoulder is wide enough and clear.
note: You must never drive off the paved or main‑traveled portion of the road to pass another vehicle, even if the shoulder looks wide, clear, or the vehicle ahead is turning. Passing must be done only within a proper lane on the roadway.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do regarding the brakes?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly immediately.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, sudden braking can make the skid worse. Instead, ease off the accelerator, stay off the brakes, and steer smoothly in the direction you want the front of the car to go until you regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Run the light quickly to avoid delay.,b:Stop,c:Honk and proceed slowly without stopping.,d:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: If your side view is blocked at an intersection, you must stop and then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions. Only proceed when you are sure cross traffic and pedestrians are clear.

question: If stopping on snow or ice and your vehicle has ABS, you should:
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and let the car drift to a stop.,d:Use the parking brake instead of the foot brake.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup, allowing you to steer while braking hard, even on snow or ice.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:You can see all blind spots using rearview mirrors.,b:Blind spots don't exist for small cars.,c:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,d:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors and must check by turning your head. Large trucks have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger vehicles, so you should avoid lingering alongside or close behind them.

question: Which is true about driving after taking medications?
options: a:Many over-the-counter cold medicines can cause drowsiness and impair driving.,b:All over-the-counter medicines are safe at recommended doses.,c:Prescription medications never impair driving if prescribed by a doctor.,d:Medications cannot affect experienced drivers.
note: Many over‑the‑counter and prescription medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read labels and talk with your doctor or pharmacist to understand how a medication may affect your ability to drive safely.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, which lights help other drivers see you best?
options: a:Turn up the instrument panel lights.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Turn on your parking lights.
note: In reduced visibility such as dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights so others can see you more easily. In many states, if your windshield wipers are on, your headlights are legally required to be on as well.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are required to affect driving ability?
options: a:It takes at least two drinks.,b:Alcohol has no effect if eaten with food.,c:Even one drink can impair driving.,d:Three drinks are required to impair driving.
note: Even one alcoholic drink can slow your reaction time and affect judgment and coordination. Any amount of alcohol can make driving less safe, so you should not assume a small amount is harmless.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a lighted intersection, whose instructions do you follow?
options: a:Honk at the officer.,b:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.,c:Follow the directions given by the officer.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s hand signals and instructions, even if they are different from the traffic lights or signs. The officer’s directions temporarily override normal traffic controls.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Continue at the same speed and stay in your lane.,c:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop.,d:Stop immediately even if you are inside an intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and flashing lights, you must yield by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, how should you respond?
options: a:Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway, even when there is no marked crosswalk.

question: When must you use your low beam headlights?
options: a:When in fog, snow, rain, or other conditions that reduce visibility, and at night when you are driving behind or meeting other traffic.,b:Only on unlit roads.,c:Only when another vehicle is approaching.,d:When parked on the shoulder at night.
note: Use low beam headlights whenever visibility is reduced by weather such as fog, rain, or snow, or any other condition that makes it hard to see the road or other vehicles. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and make it even harder to see, so low beams are safer in these conditions and at night when other traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a curve, when should you slow down?
options: a:In the middle of the curve.,b:After you have completed the curve.,c:Before entering the curve.,d:Only if a sign indicates to do so.
note: You should slow down before you enter a curve. Braking while already in the curve can cause you to lose traction and control, especially at higher speeds. Enter the curve at a safe speed, then maintain a steady speed through it.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of at least what percent?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers 21+ are legally impaired at 0.08% BAC or higher and face criminal penalties for DUI.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Use only the shoulder belt.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,d:Wear the shoulder belt behind your back.
note: If your vehicle has both a lap belt and a shoulder belt, you must wear both. The lap belt should fit low and snug across your hips, and the shoulder belt should go over your chest and away from your neck. Using both together keeps you from sliding under the belt and reduces the risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: When driving at night, what is a recommended safety practice?
options: a:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,b:Always use high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increasing your following distance at night gives you more time to react because visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge speed and distance. You should also avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights and use your high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you cannot find a gap to enter the freeway, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Adjust your speed on the ramp to match freeway traffic and merge into a safe gap.,b:Back up on the ramp to a merge point.,c:Maintain your speed and force others to make room.,d:If you reach the end of the ramp with no safe gap, stop and wait until traffic clears.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, you should adjust your speed in the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic and merge into a safe gap. If you reach the end of the ramp and still cannot find a safe gap, you must stop and wait until traffic clears enough to merge safely. Never back up on the ramp or force your way into traffic.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Driving very slowly.,c:The number of passengers in the vehicle.
note: Aggressive drivers often show unsafe behaviors such as erratic, frequent, or improper lane changes, tailgating, and failing to yield. These sudden moves increase crash risk, so you should give them space and avoid engaging with them.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Leave the wheels unlocked so they can roll.,b:Turn them straight ahead.,c:Turn them to the right,d:Turn them left toward the center of the road.
note: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the side of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic.
