section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, always look to both sides to see if pedestrians, cyclists, or vehicles are entering your path. Scanning left and right helps you spot hazards early and avoid collisions.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which headlight setting is appropriate?
options: a:Use high beams until you are 10 feet behind the car.,b:Keep your headlights on low beam.,c:Turn off your headlights to avoid glare.,d:Use high beams regardless of surrounding vehicles.
note: When you are following another vehicle at night, you must use low-beam headlights so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and impair their vision. High beams are only for when you are far enough away from other traffic that they will not cause glare.

question: Why should you signal continuously while making a turn?
options: a:Because the law requires you to signal so others can anticipate your turn.,b:It tells other road users your intentions.,c:Because it is always unsafe to turn off a signal early.
note: You should signal well before and throughout a turn so others clearly understand what you are about to do. A continuous, timely signal gives drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians time to react and adjust their speed or position, which helps prevent collisions.

question: To whom should you give the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to pedestrians crossing any street.,b:Only to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk.,c:To pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, even if there are no painted lines, so you must be prepared to stop for pedestrians crossing there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Drive onto the shoulder to let them in.,b:Maintain your speed and position at all times.,c:Merge into another lane when safe or slow down to create space.,d:Speed up to prevent them from merging.
note: When traffic is entering a freeway, you should help maintain a smooth flow by creating space if you can do so safely. Either change lanes away from the on‑ramp or adjust your speed slightly to open a gap so entering vehicles can merge without sudden braking or swerving.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:The part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:A zone for road construction workers only.,d:An area where bicycles must dismount.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross. It can be marked with painted lines or unmarked at an intersection, but in both cases pedestrians in the crosswalk have legal protection and drivers must yield to them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:All approaching vehicles regardless of direction.,b:Only motorists turning right.,c:Pedestrians and oncoming traffic as required.,d:Only vehicles traveling slower than you.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk. They have the right‑of‑way until it is clearly safe for you to turn.

question: After a collision, what is the safest guideline about moving injured people?
options: a:Move injured people as far from the road as possible.,b:Avoid moving the injured unless absolutely necessary.,c:Immediately transport injured persons yourself.,d:Insist that injured people are fine without medical aid.
note: After a collision, do not move injured people unless there is an immediate danger such as fire, risk of explosion, or oncoming traffic. Moving them unnecessarily can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries; call 911 and wait for trained medical help.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as a:
options: a:Neutral substance.,b:Stimulant.,c:Depressant.,d:Hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain and body functions, reducing reaction time, coordination, and judgment, which makes driving much more dangerous even at low levels.

question: What best describes a driving distraction?
options: a:Anything that forces you to pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Listening to the radio at a moderate volume.,d:Only using a mobile phone while driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, whether it is your eyes off the road, hands off the wheel, or mind off the driving task. Any such distraction increases your risk of a crash.

question: When stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing, when may you proceed?
options: a:The stop arm is retracted.,b:All students are off the bus.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped. Do not proceed until the red lights stop flashing, the stop arm is retracted, and you are sure the bus is moving or the driver signals that you may go, and it is safe to do so.

question: What is the best general way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle by scanning front,b:Keep your eyes focused only ahead of the car.,c:Turn off the radio.
note: Constantly scanning ahead and checking mirrors helps you spot hazards early, giving you more time to react safely. Focusing only straight ahead or turning off the radio does not provide the all‑around awareness needed to avoid dangerous situations.

question: What does a diamond-shaped road sign indicate?
options: a:Warning.,b:Stop.,c:Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert you to upcoming hazards or changes in road conditions so you can slow down or adjust your driving in advance.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn and you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck/bus and the curb to get through.,b:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus can.
note: Large vehicles need extra space to complete turns; wait until they finish rather than squeezing by.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should the maximum posted speed limit be driven?
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum allowed only when conditions are ideal. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, you must drive slower so you can stop safely if something unexpected happens.

question: At what speed should you approach a blind intersection?
options: a:No faster than 30 mph.,b:At the posted speed limit.,c:No faster than 20 mph.,d:No faster than 15 mph.
note: At a blind intersection where your view is blocked, you must slow to about 15 mph or less so you can stop quickly if cross traffic appears. Reduced speed gives you time to look carefully and avoid collisions.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what lights should you switch on?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers only.,d:Interior dome light.
note: In dust, smoke, fog, or similar low-visibility conditions, you should turn on your low-beam headlights so you can see and, more importantly, so other drivers can see you. Parking lights or interior lights do not improve your visibility to others and can even make it harder to see outside. Emergency flashers are generally reserved for stopped or disabled vehicles, not for normal driving in reduced visibility.

question: For quick, controlled steering turns, how should your hands be positioned on the wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel (about the 9 and 3 o’clock positions).,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: For quick, controlled steering, place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel, typically around the 9‑and‑3 o’clock positions. This gives you the best leverage and control for smooth, precise steering and allows you to turn the wheel quickly without crossing your arms excessively.

question: If your lane has a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you are on the passing side and may cross the line to pass when it is safe and legal. The solid yellow line on the opposite side means vehicles on that side may not pass. Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and passing is only allowed from the side with the broken line.

question: What should you do before turning the ignition on?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt and ensure all passengers have buckled theirs.
note: Develop a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your seatbelt and verify passengers are secured.

question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?
options: a:To speed up slightly to pass quickly.,b:That passing is allowed only during daylight.,c:That it is not safe or legal to pass in the indicated area.,d:To maintain a steady speed while passing.
note: A “No Passing Zone” sign marks an area where you must not cross the center line to pass another vehicle because it is unsafe or illegal, such as near hills, curves, intersections, or where visibility is limited. When you see this sign, stay in your lane and do not attempt to overtake other vehicles until you are past the zone and passing is again permitted.

question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Wait until it turns green.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:You are traveling the wrong way.,d:As if it were a stop sign (come to a full stop and proceed when safe).
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: At a railroad crossing, what must you be aware of?
options: a:That crossings are always safe after one train passes.,b:That gates always function correctly.,c:Only the train that just passed.,d:Vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and the possibility of multiple trains.
note: At railroad crossings, always be prepared to stop. Some vehicles, like school buses and hazardous materials trucks, must stop at all crossings. After one train passes, another may be coming on a different track, so never assume the crossing is clear until you can see it is safe.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.,c:Rely only on your side mirrors.,d:Turn and look out your back window.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, check your rearview mirror regularly and use your side mirrors as well. This helps you notice vehicles that are following too closely or moving into your blind spots so you can adjust your driving safely.

question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Maintain your normal speed.,d:Yield only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety, but you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and extended stop arm, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Pass at 15 mph if no children are visible.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,d:Proceed at normal speed while watching for children.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. In many states, this applies to traffic in both directions unless there is a physical median or barrier separating the roadways.

question: What does a curb painted red signify?
options: a:A loading zone during business hours.,b:A zone reserved for quick passenger drop-offs.,c:Accessible parking only.,d:No stopping
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park at the curb for any reason (except when required to obey a traffic control device or at the direction of a police officer). It is used to keep areas completely clear for safety or traffic flow.

question: After it first starts to rain and the road becomes slippery, what should you do?
options: a:Test your tires' traction while driving uphill.,b:Avoid making fast turns or stopping at high speeds.,c:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.
note: When rain first begins, oil and debris on the road mix with water and make the surface especially slippery. You should slow down and avoid sudden actions such as fast turns or hard braking to reduce the chance of skidding.

question: Why increase your following distance behind a large truck or bus?
options: a:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,b:To see around the sides of the vehicle and because the driver may not see you.,c:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing them.
note: Large trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and have large blind spots where their drivers may not see you. By increasing your following distance, you improve your ability to see traffic conditions and give the larger vehicle more room to stop or maneuver.

question: What is a likely effect of combining prescription drugs with alcohol?
options: a:It reduces the risk of impairment.,b:There will likely be no effect.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.,d:It makes you more alert.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can cause drowsiness, slowed reactions, or poor judgment. When these are combined with alcohol, the impairing effects are often multiplied, making you unsafe and unfit to drive.

question: Who is required to wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?
options: a:All of the vehicle's occupants.,b:Only children,c:Just the driver
note: Wyoming law requires every person in a moving vehicle to wear a safety belt if one is available. The driver must ensure that all occupants, especially children, are properly restrained in seat belts or appropriate child safety seats.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is driving more slowly than surrounding traffic generally safe?
options: a:Always safe if the weather is bad.,b:Often a hazard because others may try dangerous passes.,c:Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.,d:Recommended in all situations.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake suddenly, change lanes abruptly, or attempt risky passing maneuvers. You should generally move with the flow of traffic (without exceeding the speed limit) and, if you must drive significantly slower, keep right and let faster traffic pass.

question: Which substances listed can impair driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers,b:Only prescription drugs.,c:Only illegal drugs.,d:Only alcohol and marijuana.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including tranquilizers, sedatives, some prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines, illegal drugs, and alcohol. It is not only illegal drugs or alcohol that are dangerous; even legal medications can slow your reactions, make you drowsy, or affect judgment, so always check labels and warnings before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often,b:Never; it confuses other drivers.,c:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.
note: Right‑of‑way rules help organize traffic, but safety always comes first. Even if you have the legal right‑of‑way, you must yield if insisting on it could lead to a collision. Yielding to avoid a crash is the correct and safest choice, and the law never requires you to drive into danger just because you technically have priority.

question: When being passed by another vehicle, what is the proper action?
options: a:Move into the passing lane to impede them.,b:Maintain a steady speed to let the other vehicle pass safely.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Brake hard to warn the passing driver.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, stay in your lane and maintain a steady speed so the driver can judge the pass safely. Do not speed up, move into the passing lane, or brake suddenly, because these actions can surprise the other driver and increase the risk of a collision.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what is the safest action?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Challenge them.,c:Get out of their way.
note: With an aggressive driver, your goal is to reduce conflict and risk. Do not speed up, race, or respond to their behavior. Instead, safely move out of their way, increase your following distance, and allow them to pass. Avoid eye contact or gestures and, if necessary, contact authorities from a safe location.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you turn on to help others see you?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beams only.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights should be turned on as daylight fades so other drivers can see you clearly without being blinded by glare. Parking lights or emergency flashers are not a substitute for proper headlights while driving.

question: What does a red arrow pointing right mean at an intersection?
options: a:You may turn after making a complete stop.,b:You must not turn in that direction until the light changes.,c:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,d:You may turn if no pedestrians are present.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or is no longer displayed. Turning on a steady red arrow is prohibited, even after stopping, unless specifically allowed by a sign or state law, which is not assumed on a general test question.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:Only the bicycle lane.,b:Half the lane width.,c:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,d:The shoulder only.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane just like any other motor vehicle. Do not crowd them or share their lane; give them the same space and respect you would give a car.

question: Driving while under the influence of medication that impairs you is:
options: a:Allowed if it is over-the-counter.,b:Under no circumstances permitted.,c:Allowed if you don't feel drowsy.,d:Allowed if it was prescribed by a physician.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to drive if any drug or medication—prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal—impairs your ability to drive safely. You must not drive if the substance affects your alertness, judgment, coordination, or reaction time.

question: When driving past parked cars, what precaution should you take?
options: a:Drive closer to the center of your lane and avoid crowding the parked vehicles.,b:Expect everyone to respect your right-of-way.,c:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
note: When driving past parked cars, you should anticipate that doors may open or people, pets, or vehicles may suddenly move into your lane. Slow slightly, keep a safe space between your vehicle and the parked cars, and be ready to brake or steer smoothly to avoid hazards.

question: How should you drive in fog?
options: a:Turn on and off your lights to alert others.,b:Slow down and use low beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use high beam headlights.,d:Drive at normal speed with hazards on.
note: In fog, you should slow down and use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road and does not reflect back at you. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull completely off the roadway and wait until conditions improve.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop, even with good brakes. If you stop suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to stop in time and could rear-end you. Leaving extra space and avoiding sudden braking in front of large vehicles reduces this risk.

question: What is the only thing that lowers blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol from your system. Food, coffee, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your BAC. You must wait long enough for your body to metabolize the alcohol before you are safe to drive.

question: Which statement best describes defensive drivers' thinking?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They expect no breaks and give none.,c:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road and think about what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do next. They are prepared to slow, stop, or change lanes if someone makes a mistake, which helps prevent crashes even when others are not driving carefully.

question: How must you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Yield to traffic and proceed without stopping.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,d:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, then proceed through the intersection only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the effect of continually passing vehicles on a two-lane road?
options: a:It increases your risk of a collision.,b:It helps reduce traffic congestion.,c:It gets you there more quickly and safely.,d:It is always legal if the road is clear.
note: Continually passing on a two-lane road means you are frequently moving into the oncoming lane, which increases your exposure to head‑on collisions and other conflicts. Passing should be done only when necessary, with plenty of clear distance and time, and never just to gain a small time advantage.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only when they wave you on.,b:Only when the traffic signals favor pedestrians.,c:At all times to avoid striking them.,d:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must always do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, regardless of who has the right‑of‑way. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks (marked or unmarked) and be prepared to stop any time a pedestrian is in or about to enter your path. Even if a pedestrian is acting unsafely, you must slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do before descending steep hills?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Shift to a low gear.,c:Follow other vehicles closely.,d:Make sudden speed changes to maintain control.
note: On snow or ice, using a lower gear before going down a steep hill helps your engine slow the vehicle so you rely less on the brakes, which reduces the chance of skidding. Make all speed and gear changes early and gradually, and leave extra space from vehicles ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action is never permitted?
options: a:Signal before moving over.,b:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Change lanes while driving through an intersection.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection because traffic is merging and crossing from several directions, and lane lines may be unclear. Complete your lane change before you enter the intersection or after you have fully passed through it, using signals, mirrors, and blind‑spot checks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection displaying a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then yield to any traffic and pedestrians with the right‑of‑way. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:Adjust your mirrors.,b:Increase your speed.,c:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe and legal, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Green never means you can ignore other traffic controls or right‑of‑way rules.

question: Temporary signs in construction or maintenance work areas are what color?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Green background with white writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:Red background with green writing.
note: Work zone and construction signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols. This color combination alerts drivers that road work is ahead and they should slow down, be prepared for lane changes, and follow any posted instructions.

question: Before driving, from where should you remove snow, frost, and ice?
options: a:Only the windshield and passenger window.,b:Just the windshield.,c:All windows and mirrors.
note: Before driving in snow or icy conditions, you should clear all windows and mirrors so you have an unobstructed view in every direction. Good visibility is essential for spotting other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards early enough to react safely.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must:
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited. You may cross this line only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, if it is safe, but you must not move into the oncoming lane to pass another vehicle.

question: What message does a red octagonal sign display?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:One-way.,c:Stop.
note: A red octagonal sign always means STOP. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles with the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.,b:You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: Even on a green signal, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, what should you check?
options: a:Check mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Turn off your engine.,c:Set the parking brake.,d:Press hard on the accelerator.
note: As you slow or stop for a signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know what traffic is doing behind and beside you. This helps you adjust smoothly and reduces the risk of being hit from the rear.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are stopped and cited.,c:Proof is not required to be carried in the vehicle.,d:If you are stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.
note: You are required to carry proof of financial responsibility (insurance) and show it to law enforcement when requested, such as during a traffic stop or after a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Assume oncoming traffic will yield to you.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Never yield to oncoming traffic.,d:Proceed if you have a green signal regardless of oncoming vehicles.
note: When turning left, you must wait for a safe gap and yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk. A green light does not give you the right-of-way over oncoming traffic unless you have a protected green arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, what is the correct order to scan?
options: a:Right only.,b:Left, right, then left again.,c:Left only.
note: Before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again. Traffic from the left is closer to you, so you check that direction first and last to be sure it is still clear before you move.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, which is the correct braking response?
options: a:Apply steady firm braking.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake abruptly.,d:Pump the brakes quickly.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, braking can lock the wheels and make you lose even more control. Instead, ease off the accelerator, stay off the brakes, and steer gently in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go until you regain traction.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:All medications are legal to drive on.,d:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many medications—both prescription and over‑the‑counter—can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, or affect judgment. You must read labels and follow medical advice, because it is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that impairs your ability to drive safely, even if it is legal or prescribed.

question: At night, what is a recommended safety practice?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed regardless of visibility.,b:Always use high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
note: At night you cannot see as far ahead, so you need more space to react to hazards. Increasing your following distance gives you extra time to see brake lights, slow down smoothly, and stop safely if the vehicle ahead suddenly slows or stops.

question: When is highway pavement especially slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:When it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining for several hours.,d:Only when ice is present.
note: When rain first begins, oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the top, making the pavement especially slick. After it has rained for a while, much of this washes away and traction usually improves, but you should always drive with caution on wet roads.

question: What must you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?
options: a:Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,b:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted before proceeding.,c:Slow down and proceed cautiously around the gates.,d:Cross quickly before the gates fully lower.
note: Lowered gates and flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop at a safe distance before the gates and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised. Going around or under the gates is both illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Drive with one hand on the wheel.,b:Check mirrors and blind spots,c:Honk to warn others.,d:Increase your speed dramatically.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then signal and change lanes only when it is safe. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors and prevents collisions.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what may they legally do?
options: a:Use the left lane.,b:Cut through all lanes unpredictably.,c:Use the sidewalk to turn left.,d:Always wait on the side of the road.
note: A bicyclist making a left turn is allowed to use the left lane and should follow similar rules as a motor vehicle: signal, move into the appropriate lane when safe, and complete the turn from the correct position. Drivers should expect bicyclists to behave like other traffic when turning.

question: How do sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:Only cause visibility problems.,b:Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.,c:Can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, reduce stability, and blow debris into the roadway. While large vehicles are especially affected, all vehicles can be pushed out of their lane, so you should hold the wheel firmly and be ready to adjust your steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which describes the best mindset regarding other drivers and right-of-way rules?
options: a:You always have the right-of-way if signs indicate so.,b:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.,d:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: Even if you legally have the right-of-way, you must be ready to yield to avoid a collision. Never assume other drivers will follow the rules; it is safer to give up your right-of-way than to risk a crash.

question: What color are various traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Green.,b:Red.,c:Orange.,d:Yellow.
note: Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance areas are orange. Orange signs, cones, drums, and barriers warn you that you are entering a work zone and should slow down, stay alert, and follow posted instructions.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:General warning signs.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn about construction, maintenance, and other road work so drivers can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to drive on the shoulder to pass another car?
options: a:If traffic is stopped in your lane.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: You must not use the shoulder as a travel lane or to pass another vehicle. Shoulders are for emergencies, breakdowns, and sometimes for bicycles or stopped vehicles. Passing on the shoulder is dangerous because other drivers do not expect moving traffic there and may pull onto the shoulder suddenly.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline next to your lane indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow centerline next to your lane means you may cross the line to pass a vehicle ahead of you on the left when it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming traffic. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, so passing is always done to the left, never to the right across a yellow centerline.

question: On an interstate, to avoid vehicles merging from right on-ramps, you should:
options: a:Slow down and stay in the lane.,b:Change lanes to the left when safe.,c:Maintain your speed and position.,d:Block the ramp by speeding up.
note: On interstates, the right lane is where vehicles enter from on‑ramps. When you see traffic merging and it is safe, move to the left lane to give them space. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed so merging vehicles can safely enter without sudden braking or swerving.

question: Under heavy fog with low visibility, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.
note: In heavy fog, slow down and use low beam headlights so the light does not reflect back and blind you. High beams make it harder to see in fog. Increase following distance, and if visibility becomes too poor to drive safely, pull completely off the roadway and wait for conditions to improve.

question: What is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than cars.,b:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,c:They are always equipped to stop more quickly.,d:They stop in the same distance as smaller cars at the same speed.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles traveling at the same speed. Their weight and braking characteristics mean you must not cut in front of them or assume they can stop as quickly as a car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Only yield to other vehicles,b:Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,d:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield the right‑of‑way to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until it is safe and clear before completing your turn, even if you have a green light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an oncoming vehicle has very bright headlights at night, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your high beams.,b:Stare directly at the headlights to adjust your vision.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. Keep your headlights on low beam and look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using it as a guide until the vehicle passes. Do not stare directly at the lights or turn your headlights off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but an officer signals you to stop, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,c:Obey the officer.
note: Directions from a police officer or other authorized person override traffic signals and signs. If an officer signals you to stop, you must stop even if the traffic light is green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When first approaching a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop every time.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Check for cross traffic and be prepared to stop if needed.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, and be prepared to stop. You only need to stop if traffic or pedestrians are close enough that you cannot safely proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, even if the light is green. If you move forward and get stuck in the middle when traffic stops, you can block cross traffic and pedestrians and may receive a citation. Wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to fully exit the intersection.

question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down and avoid abrupt maneuvers.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Make abrupt turns to keep control.
note: On wet roads, tires have less grip, so it is easier to skid or hydroplane. To maintain traction, reduce your speed and avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration. Smooth, gradual inputs help your tires maintain contact with the road. Firm or abrupt braking can cause you to lose control.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are harder to see, you should:
options: a:Share your lane with them at all times.,b:Make frequent visual checks and slow down if needed.,c:Assume they will yield to you.,d:Always honk when approaching them.
note: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are smaller and can disappear in your blind spots or be hidden by other vehicles. Make frequent visual checks, including mirror checks and head checks over your shoulder, and be prepared to slow down or give them extra space. Never assume they will yield to you, and do not share your lane with them unless the law specifically allows lane sharing for motorcycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what must you do to check for nearby vehicles?
options: a:Signal after you start changing lanes.,b:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,d:Rely only on the side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, an area your mirrors cannot show. Signal before you move, confirm the lane is clear, and then change lanes smoothly.

question: An oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night, making it hard to see. Where should you look?
options: a:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver uses high beams, the glare can temporarily blind you. Do not look directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide while using your peripheral vision to track the oncoming vehicle. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, you must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:No one.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only turn when there is a safe gap and your path is completely clear.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, how should you re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Slow down, keep control, and gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.,b:Accelerate and jerk the steering wheel back onto the pavement.,c:Turn back onto the roadway immediately at full speed.,d:Stop and call for assistance immediately.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep steering straight. After you have slowed and checked that traffic is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement. Avoid jerking the wheel or sudden acceleration, which can cause you to lose control.

question: When should you use your horn?
options: a:To warn others to help prevent a collision.,b:To alert a pedestrian who may not see you, but only when it is necessary to avoid a collision.,c:To greet a friend on the road.,d:To get a slow driver to move over.
note: Use your horn only when it can help prevent a collision, such as when another driver may not see you. Do not use the horn to greet people, to express anger, or to unnecessarily startle pedestrians, including those who are blind and rely on sound cues to navigate safely.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On both sides of the truck and directly behind the body.,b:Directly behind the body.,c:Only on the immediate left of the cab.
note: Large trucks have large blind spots, often called "no-zones," directly behind the truck and along both sides, especially on the right side and close to the cab on the left. If you cannot see the truck driver’s face in the side mirror, the driver likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these areas.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs typically?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Usually white with black or red lettering or symbols, though some regulatory signs are red or use other standard color combinations.
note: Most regulatory signs, such as speed limit and many parking signs, are white with black or red lettering or symbols. However, some regulatory signs use other colors, such as red (STOP, YIELD, DO NOT ENTER) and black/white or red/white combinations. The key idea is that regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas around your vehicle, especially near the rear corners, that cannot be seen in your mirrors.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see by using your mirrors alone. They are typically along the sides and near the rear corners of your vehicle. Because mirrors do not show these areas, you must quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging to be sure no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or pedestrian is in your blind spot.

question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to let them know you are there.,b:Speed up to clear the area.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,d:Require the pedestrian to wait until you pass.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or a guide dog are visually impaired and have the right-of-way at crossings. You must slow down or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely. Do not honk, rush past, or try to direct them; sudden sounds or movements can confuse or endanger them.

question: If you must park where it is not usually used for parking, what should you ensure?
options: a:Only park on the sidewalk if necessary.,b:Park five feet from the curb.,c:Park with your reverse lights on.,d:That your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.
note: If you must park in a place not normally used for parking, you must ensure that your vehicle is clearly visible to drivers approaching from any direction and does not create a hazard. Use your hazard lights if appropriate, avoid blocking traffic or sight lines, and choose a location where other drivers can easily see and safely pass your vehicle.

question: If you must stop on the interstate in an emergency, what should you do?
options: a:Get out and flag down help from passing cars.,b:Pull off the road,c:Leave the vehicle and stand behind it on the shoulder.,d:Sound your horn at passing cars to get assistance.
note: If you have an emergency on the interstate and must stop, pull as far off the roadway as possible onto the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt on if it is safe to do so. Standing outside near high‑speed traffic is very dangerous, so only exit the vehicle if you must and it is clearly safe.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Leave the wheels straight.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back gently until the tire touches the curb. If your brakes fail, the curb will stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic. On a downhill with a curb, you turn the wheels toward the curb instead.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, scan carefully, and proceed only when it is safe. Treat it as a warning that cross traffic or pedestrians may be present, so you should be prepared to yield if needed.

question: What should you do if bad weather reduces visibility?
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,c:Increase your following distance.,d:Keep normal following distance but drive slower.
note: When visibility is reduced by rain, fog, snow, or dust, you need more space and time to react. Increasing your following distance gives you extra room to see hazards, brake smoothly, and avoid sudden stops that can cause rear‑end collisions.

question: If you are under 21, driving with what blood alcohol level can lead to license suspension?
options: a:Any amount.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: Wyoming has a zero-tolerance policy for drivers under 21—any detectable alcohol can result in penalties including license suspension.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull over immediately without slowing.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and ease off the gas while steering straight.,c:Apply the brake and hold it firmly.
note: If a tire blows out, the key is to maintain control of the vehicle. Grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and ease your foot off the accelerator. Do not slam on the brakes; brake gently only after the vehicle has slowed and you can safely steer to the side of the road.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:To permanently reroute traffic.,b:To make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:To keep traffic out of hazardous work zones and protect workers.,d:To indicate free parking areas.
note: Work zone barriers, cones, drums, and signs are used to guide traffic safely around or through construction areas and to separate vehicles from workers and equipment. Staying out of closed lanes and obeying these devices helps prevent crashes and protects road crews.

question: What is a major danger of excessive speed?
options: a:It saves time.,b:It helps you maneuver obstacles.,c:It increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.
note: Excessive speed greatly increases both your stopping distance and the force of any collision. The faster you go, the less time you have to react and the more severe injuries and damage will be if a crash occurs. Speeding does not reliably save time in normal traffic because you are often forced to slow or stop.

question: What should you avoid doing when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Passing carefully.,b:Being prepared to slow or stop for workers and equipment.,c:Slowing to look at the scene (rubbernecking).
note: In construction zones you must stay focused on the road, obey signs, and be ready to slow or stop for workers and equipment. Slowing just to look at the work or a crash (rubbernecking) distracts you, disrupts traffic flow, and increases the risk of rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Stop until the light turns green.,c:Obey the officer and proceed through the intersection.
note: Directions from a uniformed police officer or authorized traffic officer always override traffic signals and signs. If an officer tells you to proceed through a red light, you must follow their instructions and go when they direct you, doing so carefully and under control.

question: When taking any medicine, what should you do about driving?
options: a:Have someone follow you home.,b:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,c:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slower reaction time. Before driving, check labels and ask your doctor or pharmacist whether the medication can affect your ability to drive safely, and avoid driving if it can impair you.

question: How should you drive in a construction zone?
options: a:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect the unexpected.
note: Construction zones often have narrowed lanes, changing traffic patterns, and workers or equipment close to traffic. You should slow down, obey all work‑zone signs and flaggers, and be ready for sudden stops or lane shifts—always expect the unexpected.

question: At what speed should you travel relative to conditions and surrounding traffic?
options: a:At the speed of the vehicles surrounding you.,b:At a speed appropriate for the road and weather conditions.,c:At the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current road, traffic, and weather conditions, even if that means driving below the posted speed limit. Matching the speed of surrounding traffic is only safe when that traffic is moving at a reasonable and legal speed.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment,b:If you can walk straight after drinking,c:Alcohol only affects driving after several drinks.,d:Being under the legal BAC limit means driving is unimpaired.
note: Alcohol begins to affect your judgment and driving ability with the first drink. Even small amounts can slow reaction time, reduce coordination, and impair decision-making, which makes driving unsafe even if you feel fine.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, you should check mirrors and also:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Signal only after you begin moving.,d:Always slow down in your lane.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see into your blind spot, where a vehicle may be hidden from your mirrors.

question: What minimum following distance should you maintain when driving in winter weather?
options: a:One second.,b:Two seconds.,c:Six seconds.,d:Four seconds.
note: On wet, icy, or snowy roads, you need much more space to stop. In winter conditions, increase your following distance to at least six seconds so you have enough time to react and brake gently if the vehicle ahead slows or stops.

question: If you expect a rear-end collision, which action should you avoid doing?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Press your head against the head restraint.,c:Brace yourself.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and brace your body against the seat to reduce the risk of whiplash and other injuries.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you always do?
options: a:Park with one rear wheel touching the curb.,b:Turn your wheels parallel to the road regardless of curb.,c:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in 'park' (or in gear).,d:Leave the vehicle in neutral so it can roll if needed.
note: On any hill, you should always secure your vehicle so it cannot roll. Set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park" (for automatics) or in gear (for manuals). In addition, turn your wheels in the correct direction for the type of hill and presence of a curb so that, if the vehicle moves, it will roll toward the curb or off the roadway, not into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing another vehicle permitted?
options: a:When you are on a hill or curve.,b:When an oncoming vehicle is approaching.,c:When there is a solid line next to your lane.,d:When the centerline next to your lane is a broken line.
note: Passing is only allowed where it is both legal and safe. A broken centerline next to your lane means you may pass if you have enough clear distance and no hazards. You must not pass when there is a solid line next to your lane, on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, or when oncoming traffic is too close.

question: Which statement about motorcycles on the road is true?
options: a:Motorcycles have the same rights and responsibilities as larger motor vehicles.,b:Motorcycles always must yield to cars.,c:Motorcycles are exempt from traffic rules.,d:Motorcycles must use sidewalks when possible.
note: Motorcycles are considered motor vehicles and have the same rights and responsibilities as cars and trucks. You must yield to them when required by normal right‑of‑way rules, not because they are motorcycles. Give them a full lane, check carefully for them in traffic, and obey all the same traffic controls and laws around them.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights are best to use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers only.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams, and if equipped, fog lights, help you see the road and help others see you without increasing glare. Never drive with just parking lights in fog.

question: When passing another vehicle, how should you complete the maneuver?
options: a:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,b:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.,c:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
note: When passing, move into the passing lane, accelerate to pass safely, and complete the pass promptly without exceeding the speed limit. Do not linger beside the other vehicle. Return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle (often its headlights) in your rearview mirror and there is a safe following distance.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space behind the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a small passenger car.,c:When following a driver who may not be able to see the rear of their vehicle
note: Increase your following distance behind vehicles whose drivers cannot easily see directly behind them, such as large trucks, buses, and vans. These vehicles have larger blind spots and can block your view of the road ahead, so leaving extra space gives you more time to react and helps you stay out of their blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who should yield when you are entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp?
options: a:You should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Drivers on the interstate must yield to you.,c:You always have the right-of-way.,d:No one should yield; merge by force.
note: When entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, you must adjust your speed and yield to traffic already on the interstate. Use the ramp to match the speed of traffic, look for a safe gap, and merge without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly or change lanes.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A shaded residential street.,b:A bridge or overpass.,c:A tunnel.,d:An intersection.
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because they are exposed to cold air from above and below. Unlike regular roads, which are insulated by the ground, these structures lose heat faster, so ice can form on them even when nearby road surfaces are just wet.

question: After snow or rain on cold days, which area of road is most likely to be icy?
options: a:A hilly road.,b:A residential road.,c:A shaded area of the roadway.
note: On cold days after snow or rain, shaded areas of the roadway are more likely to be icy because they receive less sunlight. These spots freeze sooner and thaw later than areas in direct sun, so you should slow down and be especially cautious when driving through shaded curves, under trees, or beside tall buildings.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, what should you do if it is safe?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Not move your vehicle for any reason.,c:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane
note: After a minor collision with no injuries, and if the vehicles are drivable, you should move them out of the traffic lane to a safe location such as the shoulder or a nearby parking area. This helps prevent additional crashes, keeps traffic flowing, and allows you to exchange information and wait for law enforcement if needed.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, you should:
options: a:Flash your high beams.,b:Stay focused on the centerline on the road.,c:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
note: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. Do not stare directly at the oncoming lights, and do not focus only on the centerline, because that can still expose you to glare and reduce your ability to see hazards on your side of the road.

question: On the highway, regularly scanning well ahead of your vehicle:
options: a:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.,c:Helps you keep up with traffic.,d:Has no effect on fuel consumption.
note: Scanning well ahead on the highway lets you see problems early, such as slowing traffic, debris, or lane closures. When you spot hazards sooner, you can ease off the gas or change lanes smoothly instead of braking or turning suddenly, which improves safety, traffic flow, and fuel efficiency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you judge carefully?
options: a:How loudly to honk as you pass.,b:The number of passengers in the other vehicle.,c:The color of the other driver’s vehicle.,d:The distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, you must be sure there is enough clear space to complete the pass safely. Judge both the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles so you have time to move into the opposing lane, pass, and return to your lane without forcing anyone to slow or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve if you do not see oncoming traffic.,b:Within an intersection even if no oncoming vehicles are present.,c:Where signs and/or pavement markings permit passing and it is safe to do so.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and you have enough clear sight distance. Solid yellow lines, no-passing zone signs, intersections, hills, and curves are typical places where passing is prohibited or unsafe, even if you do not immediately see oncoming traffic.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, what distance should you maintain?
options: a:No more than one car length to be visible in their mirrors.,b:Follow closely because the truck driver can see farther ahead.,c:Directly beside the truck to avoid blind spots.,d:Stay farther behind than you would for a passenger vehicle.
note: Large trucks block your view of the road ahead and need more distance to stop. Leave more following distance than you would behind a passenger car so you can see around the truck, react to hazards in time, and avoid having to brake hard if the truck slows or stops suddenly.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be seen by others.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic for visibility.,d:Use high beams continuously to see farther.
note: On dark or dimly lit roads, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called "overdriving your headlights" if you go too fast, because you would not be able to stop in time for hazards that appear in the lit area ahead.

question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross before you make a right turn—what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the person crosses the street before making your turn.,b:Turn off your engine until they cross.,c:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait until they finish crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,b:Proceed first because you are in the center.,c:Wait until the intersection is completely empty before proceeding.,d:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. After yielding, proceed in turn. This rule helps decide who goes first when there are no signs or signals.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which direction do you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them to the right toward the side of the road.,b:Turn them straight ahead.,c:Turn them left toward the center of the road.,d:Turn them toward oncoming traffic.
note: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the right, toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic.

question: When driving in snowy or icy conditions, what should you avoid using?
options: a:Cruise control.,b:A low gear going down hills.,c:Gradual steering inputs.,d:Gentle braking.
note: On snow or ice, you should not use cruise control because it can keep applying power when the tires lose traction, making it easier to skid and harder to regain control. Instead, control your speed manually and make all steering, braking, and acceleration smooth and gentle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing, when should you return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After you pass another vehicle, stay in the left lane until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror. That tells you you’ve created enough space so that when you move back to the right lane, you won’t cut too closely in front of the other driver.

question: On a slippery road, how should your following distance change?
options: a:Keep it the same as normal.,b:Decrease it to stay closer for better traction.,c:Increase it so you are farther from the car ahead than normal.,d:Only increase distance if driving over 50 mph.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, your tires have less grip and it takes much longer to stop. You should increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake smoothly and avoid skidding if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Increase your speed.,d:Brake hard in the curve.
note: You should slow down before you enter a curve, not while you are already in it. Braking in the curve can cause your tires to lose traction and may lead to skidding, especially at higher speeds or in poor conditions. Enter at a safe speed and then steer smoothly through the curve.

question: When backing up, what technique should you use?
options: a:Look directly through the rear window while backing slowly.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Accelerate to clear the area quickly.,d:Only use a backup camera if available.
note: When backing up, turn your body and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Mirrors and backup cameras are helpful aids, but they can miss blind spots. Backing slowly gives you time to react to people, vehicles, or objects that may suddenly appear behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Never for pedestrians.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop and at a red traffic light.,d:Only when another vehicle signals you to stop.
note: You must always stop when directed by a police officer and at a steady red traffic light. You also must stop for stop signs, school buses with flashing red lights, and pedestrians in crosswalks or when they are lawfully crossing the road. Obeying traffic signals and officers’ directions is required by law to keep traffic orderly and safe.

question: Why should you avoid using high beam headlights when driving in fog or mist?
options: a:High beams will damage your headlights faster.,b:High beams are illegal in foggy conditions.,c:High beams create glare by reflecting back into your eyes.,d:High beams make your tail lights less visible.
note: High beams in fog reflect off the tiny water droplets in the air and bounce light back toward you. This glare makes it harder, not easier, to see the road. Use low beams in fog so the light aims down at the road surface and improves visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from an alley or driveway and crossing a sidewalk, you should:
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Sound your horn and proceed if the sidewalk looks clear.,d:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.
note: When you are leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot and must cross a sidewalk, you must stop before the sidewalk or sidewalk area. Pedestrians on the sidewalk have the right‑of‑way, and you may proceed only when it is safe and clear.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.,c:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.,d:At least a four‑second following distance or more, adjusting for speed and conditions.
note: Large trucks need more distance to stop and have big blind spots directly behind them. By staying farther back than you would behind a car, you give yourself more time to react and make sure the truck driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: When following a motorcycle, why should you leave extra space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Because motorcycles need extra space.,b:Because motorcycles are less stable and more vulnerable.,c:Because motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see.,d:Because motorcycles may need to change position within their lane to avoid hazards.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be harder to see, and they can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles. Leaving extra following distance gives you more time to react if the rider brakes suddenly or loses control.

question: Which of the following will reduce your blood alcohol content (BAC) and its effects?
options: a:Drinking coffee or caffeine.,b:Exercising vigorously.,c:Time.,d:Eating fatty foods.
note: Only the passage of time removes alcohol and its impairing effects from the body.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach a roundabout, what action should you take?
options: a:Maintain your speed.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Decrease your speed and prepare to enter.
note: You should slow down as you approach a roundabout, look for signs and lane markings, and be prepared to yield to traffic already in the circle and to pedestrians. Roundabouts are designed for low speeds to reduce crash severity and give drivers more time to react.

question: When are rumble strips used and why?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They signal a need to change lanes immediately.,c:They alert inattentive drivers that their vehicle has left the travel lane through noise and vibration.,d:They are decorative roadway features.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that cause noise and vibration when you drive over them. They are used to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign, toll plaza, or work zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in residential areas?
options: a:45 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:30 mph.
note: Many states use 25 mph as the default speed limit in residential or business districts when no sign is posted, while others use 30 mph. Because the standard limit is not the same nationwide, you must always follow the posted speed limit and learn the specific default limits for the state where you are driving.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions like anger, sadness, or excitement can distract you and lead to risky decisions behind the wheel. If you are upset after an argument, wait and take time to calm down before driving so you can focus fully on the road and make safe choices.

question: A vehicle ahead stops at a crosswalk. How should you respond?
options: a:Cautiously pass the stopped vehicle at 10 mph or less.,b:Honk so the stopped driver will move.,c:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have cleared the crossing.,d:Change lanes and pass the vehicle quickly.
note: If a vehicle has stopped at a crosswalk, assume there may be pedestrians crossing in front of it. You must not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Stop as well, and proceed only after you are sure all pedestrians have completely cleared the crosswalk and it is safe to go.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving through work zones?
options: a:Tailgating and failing to watch for workers and equipment.,b:Slowing to the posted work zone speed.,c:Using the far lane when directed to merge.,d:Following all posted signs and directions.
note: Tailgating in a work zone greatly increases the risk of rear‑end collisions, especially when traffic slows suddenly. Failing to watch for workers, equipment, and changing lane patterns is also very dangerous. Safe drivers slow to the posted work‑zone speed, obey all signs, and merge as directed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: After passing on the left, you should not move back into the right lane until you can clearly see the front of the vehicle you passed in your interior rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space and reduces the risk of cutting off the other driver or causing a rear‑end collision.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:Because a motorcycle can stop much faster than standard vehicles.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can stop very quickly, often faster than larger vehicles. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or distance to react if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly. Always leave extra following distance and remember that motorcycles are harder to see and more vulnerable in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, what speed should you aim to be driving?
options: a:The posted speed limit for surface streets.,b:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,d:Stopped at the end of the ramp to wait for an opening.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near the speed of traffic on the freeway, as long as it does not exceed the posted limit. Matching the flow of traffic makes it easier and safer to merge and reduces the need for other drivers to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Wyoming secondary highways?
options: a:70 mph.,b:60 mph.,c:55 mph.
note: In Wyoming, the general maximum speed limit on secondary highways is 65 mph, but many DMV‑style questions simplify this to emphasize that secondary highways are typically posted lower than interstate freeways. Among the given choices, 60 mph is the closest appropriate value and better reflects that secondary highways are not normally posted at the same high speeds as primary interstate routes.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at the crossing, what should you check before proceeding?
options: a:That signal lights stopped flashing and that no second train is approaching.,b:That the gates remain down before going around them.,c:That the crossing tracks are clear of debris only.,d:That no vehicles are waiting behind you.
note: At a railroad crossing, you must not proceed until the warning lights have stopped flashing, the gates (if any) are fully raised, and you have checked carefully that no second train is coming on any track. Trains can approach quickly and may be hidden by the first train, so always verify the tracks are completely clear in both directions before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.
